parole.significato: feminine singular nominative suffixed definite article. the
parole.testo: Continues Common Albanian *-ó, which became -a after colliding with -ë in feminine words. It did remain an -o in ajo, which was formed in this period. Inherited from Proto-Albanian *háh (“the, she”), identical to the Pre-Proto-Albanian form, from Proto-Indo-European *séh₂. Related to e (“of, the, to

parole.significato: forms the feminine forms for many adjectives
parole.testo: From Proto-Albanian *-jā, from Proto-Indo-European *-ih₂ ~ *-yéh₂s.

parole.significato: masculine singular nominative suffixed definite article: the
parole.testo: Continues Common Albanian *í ~ ý, from Proto-Albanian *íh ~ hýh, identical to the Pre-Proto-Albanian form, from Proto-Indo-European *ís ~ sós. Potentially cognate with Messapic -aihi. Related to i (“of, the, to”), and found in ai (“he”).
From Proto-Albanian *-sta-, from Proto-Indo-European *-stā. Unrelated to Slavic -ište as it developed from Proto-Slavic *-išče.

parole.significato: -ment (suffixed to verbs to create a noun or result)
parole.testo: From Proto-Albanian *-mā, from Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥.

parole.significato: Forms verbs from nouns, adjectives, adverbs and verbs.
parole.testo: From Old Albanian -onj, from Late Proto-Albanian *-ånje/a, from earlier *-ānja, from Late Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂nyeti.

parole.significato: used to form a secondary suffix
parole.testo: from Proto-Albanian *-us- from Proto-Indo-European *-wes-.

parole.significato: used to form verbal adjective suffix.
parole.testo: from Proto-Albanian *-tjā from Proto-Indo-European *-ti.
Derived from Proto-Albanian *-ts, from Proto-Indo-European *-ḱos.

parole.significato: used to form verbal adjective suffix.
parole.testo: From Proto-Albanian *-tāi, from Proto-Indo-European *-tós

parole.significato: Used to form a diminutive of a noun, indicating small size or youth.
parole.testo: From Proto-Albanian *-ula, from Proto-Indo-European *-ulós.

parole.significato: forms adjectives from adverbs and nouns
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Albanian *-ʉh, from Proto-Indo-European *-os.
From Proto-Albanian *-adja

From Proto-Albanian *(h)an, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂en (“there”). Cognate with Latin an (“yes, perhaps”). Interrogative particle, usually used proclitically in simple sentences.

From Proto-Albanian *atsara, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱrós, from the root *h₂eḱ- (“sharp”). Compare Old Irish aicher (“sharp, fierce, bitter”), Latin ācer (“pungent, acidic; sharp-minded”), Ancient Greek ἄκρος (ákros, “pointed, sharp; at the edge”), ἄκρον (ákron, “peak, sharp point, edge”).
From Proto-Albanian *aweisa, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂weh₁-. More at aft.
From Proto-Albanian *aweita, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂weh₁-. Compare Ancient Greek ἀῦτμη (aûtmē, “breath”), Welsh awel (“breeze”).
Inherited from Proto-Albanian *(h)aug-, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ewg- (compare Ancient Greek αὐγή (augḗ, “daylight, splendor”), Serbo-Croatian jȕg (“south”).

From Proto-Albanian *aksu-, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ó/ásku- (“workable wood”), which came to mean "red beech" in Balkan IE, from *Heh₃s- (“ash”) (compare Greek οξιά (oxiá, “beech”), Armenian հածի (haci), English ash).
From Proto-Albanian *(h)auā, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂weh₁-. See also aft.

Continuing a Common Albanian compound *aý ~ *aí, from Proto-Albanian *ahýh ~ *aíh, from a Pre-Proto-Albanian *au̯- ("away, from") + *hýh ~ íh, continuing Proto-Indo-European *h₂au̯ (“away, from”) and Proto-Indo-European *sos (“that”). The second component, from Common Albanian *ý ~ *í, is identical
From older dialectal alkë, from Proto-Albanian *alkā, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁olHk-. Compare Lithuanian álkti (“to be hungry”), Slovene lákati (“to be hungry, greedy, starving”).

Continuing a Common Albanian compound *ajó, from Proto-Albanian *au̯ + *hā́, continuing Proto-Indo-European *h₂au̯ (“away, from”) and Proto-Indo-European *sáh₂ (“that”). The second component, from Common Albanian *jó, is identical to the Albanian postponed definite article -a, which changed due to c
From Proto-Albanian *awi-mātusānj, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eyu- (“eternal”) + moshë. Cognate with Latin aeternus (“eternal”).

From Proto-Albanian *am(m)ā, perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *h₂em(m)-h₂ (compare Ancient Greek ἀμμά (ammá), Latin amma, Old High German amma) or an independently formed, sound-symbolic nursery word. Cf. also archaic Romanian îmă.
From Proto-Albanian *admā, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃od-m-éh₂ (“smell, odor”), from the root *h₃ed- (“to smell (emit an odor)”). Cognate with Ancient Greek ὀδμή (odmḗ).

parole.significato: spring, source of a spring, headwater; stream bed
parole.testo: Gheg; from Proto-Albanian *abnā (“river, riverbed”), from pre-Albanian Proto-Indo-European *h₂p-(h₃)n-éh₂, from an n-suffixed form of *h₂ep- (“body of water”). Compare Welsh afon, Old Irish aub and Latin amnis (“river”).
From Proto-Albanian *anga, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énǵʰos, from *h₂enǵʰ- (“to constrict”). Cognate to Latin angō (“to cramp (up), constrict”), German eng (“narrow”).
Deverbative of *angull, from Proto-Albanian *ankula, cognate to Greek ὀγκάομαι (ogkáomai, “to cry”) and Latin uncō (“to growl (of bears)”).
From Proto-Albanian *angarā, from *anǵʰ-n̥-reh₂, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂enh₁-ǵʰ- (compare Armenian անձն (anjn, “soul, person”), Old Norse angi (“smell, odor”)).

Cognate to tani (“now, at present, then”), from Proto-Albanian *nū, from Proto-Indo-European *nū (“now”) (cognate to Sanskrit नू (nū, “now”)). Occurs in coordination with other particles, compare nani, nime. Further related to and (Standard) Albanian a (“probably, whether; or, there”).

Enlarged with suffix -ëz, from Proto-Albanian *aunā, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ew- (“to weave”) (compare Dutch gewaad (“clothing”), Lithuanian áusti (“to weave”)). For sense development, compare Proto-Indo-European *wobʰseh₂ (“wasp”) (cf. English wasp), from *webʰ- (“to weave”) (cf. English web).

parole.significato: side (the bounding straight edge of an object)
parole.testo: With loss of -d- from archaic and dialectal ândë, from Proto-Albanian *antā, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ent- (compare English end).

From Proto-Albanian *aukn-, from possibly Proto-Indo-European *h₂euk(ʷ)-sno- (“pot”), from the root *h₂ukʷ- ~ *Hukʷ-. Cognate e.g. to Sanskrit उखा (ukhā, “pot”), Gothic 𐌰𐌿𐌷𐌽𐍃 (auhns, “oven”), English oven.
From Proto-Albanian *apa, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁op-eio/e-, from *h₁ep- (“to take”). The verb is suppletive with past dhashë and participle dhënë from Proto-Indo-European *deh₃-.
Arbëreshë; from Proto-Albanian *arga, from Proto-Indo-European *Horgʰi (compare Armenian ոջիլ (oǰil)).

parole.significato: crude pontoon raft or bridge made of wickerwork and inflated bladders
parole.testo: From older dialectal argësh, from Proto-Albanian *argusa, from Proto-Indo-European; compare Sanskrit अर्गल (argala, “bolt”), Old English reced (“building, house”).

Back-formation from plural arinj, inherited plural of Old Albanian ar 'bear', shortening of *arth, where -th was mistaken for a diminutive suffix, from Proto-Albanian *artsa, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ŕ̥tḱos. In clusters of two stops (here: tḱ), the first element (here: t) was regularly lost in Pr
From Proto-Albanian *aruā, from Proto-Indo-European *areyis-. Compare Ancient Greek ἄρυα (árua), Latvian riẽksts, Old Church Slavonic орѣхъ (orěxŭ).

From Proto-Albanian *arwā (though note the -r- instead of the expected -rr-), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂r̥h₃-wé-reh₂ (“fertile soil”), from root Proto-Indo-European *h₂erh₃- (“to plough”). Cognate to Ancient Greek ἄρουρα (ároura) and Sanskrit उर्वरा (urvarā). Possibly related to arbër, arbën (“Alb

Compare Gheg anzë (definite anza), enlarged with suffix -ëz, from Proto-Albanian *aunā, from Proto-Indo-European *Heu- (“to weave”) (compare Dutch gewaad (“clothing”), Lithuanian austi (“to weave”)). For sense development, compare Proto-Indo-European *wobʰseh₂ (“wasp”) (cf. English wasp), from *webʰ

From Proto-Albanian *aśt-, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ost(h₂-), from root *h₂st(h₂-) (“bone”); *h₃ésth₁. Cognate to Sanskrit अस्थि (ásthi-, “bone”), Ancient Greek ὀστέον (ostéon), Armenian ոսկոր (oskor).
Compound a- (“that”) + Proto-Albanian *este, cognate to Latin iste (“that”), and Lepontic 𐌉𐌑𐌏𐌔 (iśos).

From the accusative Proto-Albanian *a-ta, compound of proclitic particle a and demonstrative ta, from Proto-Indo-European *tóms, masculine accusative plural of *só m (“that (one)”) (compare Latin istud, English that). Older and dialectal varieties retain ablative asish, acish, from a + Proto-Albania

parole.significato: to file down teeth, make blunt
parole.testo: From Proto-Albanian *atˢa, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp”).

Dissectable as ath + -të. Continuing Proto-Albanian *áćuta (“provided with sharpness; sharp”), from a base *áću- (“point, sharpness”). Inherited from Proto-Indo-European *h₂óḱu- (“point, sharpness”), from the root *h₂eḱ- (“sharp”).

From Proto-Albanian *a-tā(s), compound of proclitic particle a and demonstrative tās, from Proto-Indo-European *téh₂es, feminine plural of *tód (“that (one)”) (compare Latin istud, English that). The accusative is from Proto-Albanian *a-tā(s), from earlier *a-tā(n)s, from *téh₂ns, and older and dial
From Proto-Albanian *a-tua, from Pre-Proto-Albanian *aw-tua, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂aw- + *tuó "there in the distance".
From Proto-Albanian *ata, from Proto-Indo-European *átta, whence also Hittite 𒀜𒋫𒀸 (attas), Ancient Greek ἄττα (átta), Latin atta, Proto-Slavic *otьcь, and similar Lallwörter.

Inherited from Proto-Albanian *abula, from Proto-Indo-European *n̥bʰel-, from *nébʰos (“cloud”). Closely related to Messapic atabulus. Compare Latin nebula (“mist, cloud”), Old English nifol (“mist, darkness”), Ancient Greek νεφέλη (nephélē). Compare also Romanian abur.
Verbalization of avull, from Proto-Albanian *abula, from Proto-Indo-European *nebʰ-el.

A singularized plural, based on a more archaic *bahë, from Proto-Albanian *bajā, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰew- (“to strike, beat”). Cognate with Proto-Germanic *bautaną (“to beat”) and Latin fustis (“knobbed stick, cudgel”).

From archaic and dialectal balgë, balëgë, from Old Albanian baljëgë, from Proto-Albanian *balgā, from Proto-Indo-European *bolgʷ-. Compare Greek βολβός (volvós, “bulb”), Armenian բողկ (boġk, “radish”). Borrowed as Romanian baligă; metathetic bagël gave northern Italian bagola, bagula.
From dialectal balzë, from Proto-Albanian *baldzā, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰolgʷ-. Compare Latin fulica.

parole.significato: dog or goat (with a white spot on the forehead)
parole.testo: From Proto-Albanian *bala, cognate to Lithuanian bãlas (“white”), Latvian bàls (“pale”) and Greek (Hes.) φαλός λευκός (falós lefkós), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel-.
Inherited from Proto-Albanian *balā, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰl̥h₁ós. Cognate to Old Prussian ballo (“forehead”) and Sanskrit भाल (bhāla).

From Proto-Albanian *baltā (“marsh”), hypothetically from a Proto-Indo-European *bʰolH-to- (“marsh”), originally “the white one”, a derivative of *bʰel- (“shining, white”). Cognate with Proto-Slavic *bolto (“swamp”), Lithuanian báltas (“white, shining”). Often considered an Illyrian substrate word t

From Proto-Albanian *ballā-, from Pre-Proto-Albanian *balnā-, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰólh₁neh₂- (“the white one”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel- (“shining, white”). Compare Latin flāgrāre (“to burn”), Old Church Slavonic бѣлъ (bělŭ, “white”), Lithuanian balnas (“pale”).

From Proto-Albanian *bardza, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰórh₁ǵos, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰerHǵ- (“to shine, whiten”), whence also Lithuanian brėkšti (“to dawn”), Proto-Slavic *brězgъ (“dawn, daybreak”), Proto-Germanic *berhtaz (“bright, shining”), Persian برازیدن (barâzidan, “to beautify”), Sans

parole.significato: to go for a walk, stroll
parole.testo: From Proto-Albanian *bar-otja, based on *bara (“shepherd”) (modern bari).

Back-formation from plural barinjë, from earlier *bar, from Proto-Albanian *bara, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰer- (“to carry”). Compare Old High German baro (“man, husband”). A connection with ari (“bear”) has also been proposed, though ari was originally arth prior to the loss of the -th ending by

From Proto-Albanian *báruka, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰor-uko-, from *bʰer- (“to carry”). Compare Messapic βάρυκα (báruka). A doublet of bie, barrë, and barrë. Another reconstruction is Proto-Albanian *bárkʷa-, from earlier *bʰórkʷu- "belly", from a PIE *bʰorkʷó-, from *bʰer- (“to carry”).

From Proto-Albanian *bardzmā, derived from *bardzā > bardhë (“white”), with a typical semantic pattern for the nomination of bark and bast; for a semantic parallel, compare the unrelated Proto-Slavic *lyko (“bast”) from Proto-Indo-European *lewk- (“light, shine”). A semantically close cognate is Pro

From Proto-Albanian *bárā-, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰor-áh₂ (“burden, load”), from *bʰer- (“to carry”). Cognate to Ancient Greek φορά (phorá, “burden, load”). More at bie and bark. An etymological differentiation between "burden, load" and "fetus", as desired by Orel, isn't necessary.
From Proto-Albanian *barukā, from *barwa, a derivative of berr.

From Proto-Albanian *bá(r)śtᵊkə, with r-loss before a fricative (see buzë) and postsynocopal simplification of the plosive cluster tᵊk > tk > k, from Pre-Proto-Albanian *bárśtukā-, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰórs-tu-kah₂- (“mass of hair”), collective of Proto-Indo-European *bʰorstu-kó- (“hairy”).
